title: Choose the collection contract
description: Which Java interface specifies a collection with no duplicate elements?

title: Identify transaction properties
description: Select the properties in the ACID transaction model.

title: Sum two integers
description: Read two signed integers from standard input and print their sum. Inputs are between -1000000 and 1000000.

title: Understand equals and hashCode
description: What must be true when two Java objects are equal according to equals()?
options: They must have different hash codes
They must have the same hash code
They must reference the same object

title: ConcurrentHashMap guarantees
description: Select the correct statements about ConcurrentHashMap in modern Java.
options: It supports atomic per-key operations such as compute()
It permits null keys and null values
A get() followed by put() is automatically atomic

title: Understand volatile semantics
description: Which statement best describes the volatile keyword in Java?
options: It makes compound operations such as count++ atomic
It guarantees mutual exclusion between threads
It provides visibility and ordering guarantees for accesses to the variable
It prevents garbage collection of the variable

title: Manage resources safely
description: Which interface must a Java resource implement to be used directly in a try-with-resources declaration?

title: Choose virtual threads
description: Which workload is generally best suited to Java 21 virtual threads?
options: Large numbers of concurrent blocking I/O operations

title: Java record characteristics
description: Which statements about Java records are correct?
options: Records automatically provide component accessor methods
Records automatically make referenced mutable objects deeply immutable

title: Coordinate asynchronous tasks
description: What does CompletableFuture.allOf() return?
options: The result of the fastest completed task
A CompletableFuture<Void> completed when all supplied futures complete
A list containing every task result

title: Release explicit locks
description: Why should ReentrantLock.unlock() normally be placed inside a finally block?
options: To release the lock even if the protected code throws an exception
To prevent other threads from acquiring the lock

title: Group elements with Streams
description: What is the default result structure produced by Collectors.groupingBy(classifier) in Java Streams?
options: Map of keys to lists of grouped elements

title: Filter aggregated SQL results
description: Which SQL clause filters groups after aggregation?

title: Understand LEFT JOIN
description: What does a SQL LEFT JOIN guarantee about rows from the left table?
options: All rows from the left table are retained, even without a right-side match
All rows from both tables are returned

title: Choose a composite index
description: For a PostgreSQL query filtering tenant_id by equality and created_at by a range, which B-tree index is generally the best starting point?
options: No index is ever useful for a range query

title: Rank rows with window functions
description: What does ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY department_id ORDER BY salary DESC) calculate?
options: A row number across the entire table
A rank where tied salaries receive the same number
A sequential row number restarting for each department
The total number of employees in each department

title: Understand READ COMMITTED isolation
description: Under standard READ COMMITTED isolation, which anomaly may still occur when a transaction reads the same row twice?
options: Reading a transaction's own uncommitted writes

title: Prevent SQL injection
description: Select the practices that help mitigate SQL injection and limit its impact.
options: Use prepared statements with bound parameters for untrusted values
Concatenate user input after trimming whitespace
Allow-list dynamic SQL identifiers such as sorting columns

title: Count distinct integers
description: Read an integer N followed by N space-separated integers. Print the number of distinct values. Constraints: 0 <= N <= 100000 and -1000000000 <= each value <= 1000000000.

title: Validate balanced brackets
description: Read a single line containing only the characters (), [], and {}. Print true if all brackets are correctly balanced and nested; otherwise print false. An empty string is valid. Maximum length is 100000.
